title: Dedupe replica drain events and reduce TP stall alert noise
author: Jacob Stein
release_notes: Reliability/observability: Deduplicate replica drain events emitted during TP watchdog aborts and add rate limiting for TP stall-related alerts to reduce paging noise without losing signal. No API behavior changes; error codes unchanged.
description: Context: During the 2025-02-17 TP decode hang incident and subsequent canary windows, on-call saw high alert volume from (a) repeated drain events emitted per-rank/per-loop while a wedged replica was being drained and (b) stall detectors emitting the same alerting signal at high frequency when a single replica is stuck. This PR reduces noise while preserving debuggability by deduping drain events (same replica_id + drain_reason + runtime_version) within a configurable time window and by adding a token-bucket rate limiter to a small set of high-cardinality/high-frequency TP stall notifications. Goals: keep one “this replica drained due to TP stall” event that can be correlated to request timeouts, while preventing >N duplicate events from spamming logs/metrics/alerts. Design highlights: (1) DrainEventDeduper keyed on (cluster, node, replica_id, reason, tp_world_size) with a default 10m TTL; emits a counter for suppressed duplicates; (2) Rate limiting for tp_stall_detected and tp_watchdog_fired alert-notify paths with separate buckets per (cluster, model, tp_world_size) to avoid global suppression; (3) Keep full-fidelity structured logs for the first event in a window, but downgrade subsequent ones to DEBUG with a “suppressed_by_dedupe=true” tag; (4) Preserve SRE visibility via a new metric tp_drain_event_suppressed_total and tp_stall_alert_rate_limited_total. Rollout: default enabled in canary only via runtime config; Dedicated enablement gated by SRE. Verification: replayed incident log corpus + local chaos test (forced watchdog) to confirm only one drain event per window and that paging alerts fire once per stuck replica instead of continuously. Coordination: thresholds and defaults reviewed with SRE (Rafael/Aisha) and aligned with the draft alerting plan thread.
commits: runtime/mitigation: add DrainEventDeduper with TTL cache + suppression counters
observability: add token-bucket limiter for TP stall notifier paths
logging: tag suppressed duplicates and downgrade duplicate drain logs to DEBUG
config: wire dedupe window + limiter rates to runtime config with safe defaults
tests: add unit tests for dedupe keying and limiter behavior; add integration smoke for drain flow
conversation: Rafael Mendes (review): Love the direction. Two questions: (1) what’s the dedupe key and can it accidentally collapse distinct drains (e.g., different nodes) and (2) can we ensure we still page at least once per stuck replica per 10m? The incident had cases where drains happened quickly and we still want one alert.

Jacob Stein (author): Key is (cluster, node_id, replica_id, reason, runtime_version, tp_world_size). Node is included explicitly to avoid cross-node collapse. For paging: limiter is per (cluster, model, tp_world_size) and only applies to notifier spam; the first event always emits and should page. Also added tp_stall_alert_rate_limited_total so we can see suppression rate during canary.

Aisha Bello (review): Please add a metric for “suppressed drain events” and document it in the dashboard notes. Also, default limiter rates: can we start conservative (e.g., 1/min per bucket) in canary and revisit?

Jacob Stein (author): Done. Added tp_drain_event_suppressed_total + tp_stall_alert_rate_limited_total with labels {cluster, model, tp_world_size, reason}. Defaults set to 1/min burst=2 in canary-only config; production defaults remain effectively unlimited unless enabled.

Noah Patel (review): One concern: dedupe TTL at 10m could hide a drain-loop bug if we’re thrashing (drain->restart->drain). Can we include replica incarnation / start_time in the key so a restart resets dedupe?

Jacob Stein (author): Good catch. Updated key to include replica_incarnation (monotonic counter we already bump on restart). That way drain spam within one stuck incarnation is suppressed, but a new replica lifecycle will emit again immediately.
Julian Moore (review): Please confirm that suppression only affects the “notify/pager” path and not the structured trace spans. We still need the span tags for correlation on the first event.

Jacob Stein (author): Yup. Tracing spans are unchanged; only the alert notifier + drain event emitter is deduped. First event has full structured payload and span tags; duplicates are DEBUG logs with suppressed flag.
Rafael Mendes (follow-up): Can we add a guardrail so if suppression count is high we still emit an INFO once per window that says “suppressed X duplicates”? Helps on-call understand it’s happening.
Jacob Stein (author): Added a periodic summary log at INFO at most once per TTL window per key: includes suppressed_count and first_seen/last_seen timestamps.
Aisha Bello (approval): Approved. Please coordinate enabling this with the runtime-1.19 canary plan and let SRE know the new metrics names for dashboards.
Noah Patel (approval): Approved after incarnation key change. This should materially reduce noise during stall scenarios.
merge_outcome: Merged to main; will be cherry-picked into release/runtime-1.19 after canary verification with SRE.
